verified_metadata.venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), pp. 24107–24117

metadata_sources.supports: Official proceedings title, ordered authors, June 2026 and pp. 24107–24117.
Official poster HTML identifies both authors and explicitly lists the award Highlight; cached hiddenMono_listing.html.
Confirms arXiv identifier, title, authors and cs.CV; v2 is dated 14 January 2026.
Official supplementary proofs, including sign-sorted multiplicative splitting and stabilization.

artifact.version_note: Official CVPR 2026 accepted-version PDF with CVF watermark; title, authors and printed pages checked. Official supplement also downloaded and read.

contexts.evidence: Sec. 3.1, Theorem 1: the Maxout split preserves the difference; nonnegative weights give convex monotone paired-input streams.
Secs. 3.2–3.3 stabilize both passes; the backward offsets modify sensitivities. The thesis appropriately distinguishes numerical signals from exact streams.
CVF proceedings confirms publication; the official poster page explicitly marks Highlight.
Eq. (1) and Sec. 3.1 give the max(a,b) minus b ReLU identity.
Sec. 3.1 and supplement A.1/F.1 establish the ReLU CPWL split into convex components.
Sec. 3.1 and supplement F.1 support convexity of the standard Maxout split.
Secs. 3.2–3.3 and supplement F.3 describe activation shifts and absolute-weight-product sensitivity offsets.
Sec. 4 explicitly applies the DC split to attribution.
Supplement E, Eq. (20), constructs the sign-sorted multiplicative split on nonnegative paired inputs.
Supplement E, Eq. (20), preserves differences and positive-input monotonicity. Ordinary convexity requires the thesis’s separate construction.
Sec. 4 defines SplitCAM, SplitLRP and SplitGrad; Sec. 3.5/supplement D study directly trained difference models.
Sec. 3.1 and Theorem 1 give the classical exact convex monotone paired-input representation.
The proceedings and official Highlight listing confirm the stated publication status and first-author position.
Sec. 3.1 and supplement F.1 establish convexity for the max/b pair. The stopping-decomposition comparison is the thesis’s own construction.

notes: The official supplement Appendix E overclaims ordinary convexity of posynomials. The thesis correctly restricts the inherited product construction to monotonicity on nonnegative paired inputs and supplies a separate convex construction; do not restore the stronger source claim.
The official poster page was accessible through urllib despite the browser tool failing; Highlight was verified in the actual award-name element, not inferred from navigation text.
No publisher DOI was present in the inspected official CVF record.

verified_metadata.title: Lightweight Probabilistic Deep Networks
verified_metadata.venue: 2018 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, pp. 3369–3378

metadata_sources.supports: Official CVF record verifies title, author order, CVPR 2018 and page range.
Publisher-deposited record confirms the supplied DOI, IEEE venue and pages.

artifact.version_note: Official CVPR 2018 full proceedings paper; PDF title, authors and printed pagination checked.

contexts.evidence: Sec. 3.2, Eqs. (4)–(9), propagates independent Gaussian activation means/variances in one pass. Risk aversion is the thesis’s subsequent use of these moments.
Sec. 3.2, Eq. (10b), p. 3372 gives (mu^2+sigma^2)Phi(mu/sigma)+mu sigma phi(mu/sigma)−mu_ReLU^2, not sigma^2 Phi(mu/sigma). Eq. (10a) supports the exact mean.
contexts.proposed_replacement: We propagate the exact mean $\E[\relu(X)]$ for $X \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)$~\parencite{gast2018lightweight}; in our implementation, its variance is approximated by $\sigma^2\Phi(\mu/\sigma)$.

notes: The source’s ADF propagates full closed-form Gaussian-ReLU first and second moments; its variance is not the shortcut used in the thesis implementation.
